title: Introduce downgrade-anchor and transactional migration stager for private installs
author: Ravi Patel
body:
Motivation: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers suffered two recent upgrade incidents where partial schema migrations plus out-of-band config rollbacks left clusters in a state that prevented safe downgrades. This PR adds two coordinated mechanisms to reduce blast radius and enable safe rollback when upgrades fail: (1) a lightweight downgrade-anchor metadata layer that records reversible anchors for critical migrations, and (2) a transactional migration stager operator that stages, validates, and checkpoints schema changes before they are promoted to production state.

What this changes (high level): the migration stager introduces a staging queue and preflight pipeline that runs per-tenant dry-runs, creates atomic backup checkpoints (S3/GCS or local filesystem depending on installer config), and only promotes migrations after a compatibility probe passes. The downgrade-anchor records a small, immutable metadata row per migration (anchor_id, upstream_version, checksum, rollback_script_ref) and a compatibility hint that lets the installer generate an automated rollback path when feasible. The installer CLI and terraform preflight module are extended to perform anchor verification and to refuse plans that would remove anchor-protected artifacts without an explicit release step. Helm charts include new pre-install/post-upgrade hooks that create/verify checkpoints and export anchor metadata to the operator.

Why this is different: existing guardrails focus on backups and runbook-driven rollbacks; this change creates an in-band, machine-verifiable anchor and a staging operator to reduce human error and enable safe automated rollbacks for a larger class of migrations (DDL with forward/backward compatible patterns). The design intentionally keeps the anchor compact and reversible where possible; irreversibly destructive migrations still require an explicit admin acknowledgment.

Compatibility notes: default behavior is opt-in via the installer values (private.migration.enableStager = true, private.migration.enforceAnchors = "warn"|"enforce"). For air-gapped installs, anchors are persisted to the on-disk backup directory and verified via the operator's checksum store. The change does not force any model or runtime changes for hosted customers.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for stager state machine, integration tests that run staged migrations against a local postgres instance with tenant sharding enabled, and an e2e canary test that verifies anchor-based rollback works with helm canary releases. We staged the rollout in three phases: opt-in tests, default-on for patch releases, and enforce mode 2 weeks later.

Operational runbook summary (short): 1) Run installer plan; 2) Run `installer migrate plan --staged` to generate staged plan and anchors; 3) Trigger promote once preflight passes; 4) If promote fails, run `installer migrate rollback --anchor <id>` which will attempt automated rollback using the stored rollback_script_ref and the backup checkpoint.

Related: SUP-5121 (customer incident), ENG-2893 design doc, ENG-2948 telemetry integration.

Jonah Lee: Tests look good. Suggest shrinking the default promote window to 5m from 15m for high-frequency clusters; otherwise LGTM.

release_notes: Adds a migration stager operator and a compact downgrade-anchor metadata layer. Provides staged dry-run, checkpointing, and automated rollback hooks for private installs. Opt-in by default; operator must be enabled via installer values. See docs/private/migrations.md for runbook and examples.
